newsitem.title: USA: Marriot Int'l CFO sees slow hotel building.
newsitem.headline: Marriot Int'l CFO sees slow hotel building.

text.p: Leading lodging group Marriott International Inc expects no pick up in luxury-hotel construction despite healthy occupancy rates in many markets, chief financial officer Michael Stein said on Wednesday.
Stein told an analysts meeting it was cheaper to buy existing structures, than to build new ones. Existing hotels now typically run 75 percent the cost of new construction, Stein said.
"You won't need any new supply until sometime in the future," he told the Atlanta Society of Financial Analysts.
The executive also said hotel-industry consolidation would likely continue.
Marriott International operates or franchises 1,300 hotels around the world and last month agreed to acquire the Renaissance Hotel Group, with about 150 hotels, for about $1 billion.
